title: SceneBloom: Agentic 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Zero Collisions for Embodied AI
tldr: SceneBloom combines diffusion-based layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation to produce physically realistic indoor environments. The generated scenes feature zero mesh collisions and improve real-world transfer for embodied navigation policies.
takeaways: Hierarchical sampling uses diffusion priors to generate furniture layouts within functional zones.
Contract-guided 3D compiler optimizes spatial relations to achieve zero mesh collisions and zero out-of-bounds objects.
Navigation policies trained on SceneBloom synthetic layouts outperform those trained on an equal number of real-world scans.
code: def compile_scene(diffusion_proposal, assets): relations = extract_relations(diffusion_proposal); return optimize_poses(relations, assets)
fullAnalysis: SceneBloom bridges the gap between text/image-guided generative models and physically compliant 3D simulation environments needed for embodied agent training. The framework operates in two main stages: a hierarchical diffusion sampler proposes spatial object arrangements within designated functional zones, and a contract-guided compiler translates these relational layout proposals into precise 3D object poses. By optimizing spatial contracts derived from visual priors, the compiler enforces physical validity without manual tweaking. Evaluation across five standard room types demonstrates that SceneBloom achieves superior visual realism and physical stability compared to existing baselines. Notably, it is the only framework evaluated that achieves complete elimination of object collisions and bounding errors. Furthermore, object navigation policies trained using SceneBloom generated scenes achieve higher success rates when evaluated on held-out physical scans than policies trained on equal amounts of real training environment data.

title: RobustRLlib: Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning
tldr: RobustRLlib is an algorithm-centric library and benchmark unifying 17 robust online, offline, and safe reinforcement learning algorithms under a standardized interface. It provides an extensive evaluation platform across 273 perturbation configurations to pinpoint current robustness gaps in real-world deployment scenarios. The benchmark covers advanced evaluation domains including humanoid control and vision-language-action tasks.
takeaways: Integrates 17 robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified, reusable interface.
Evaluates algorithmic resilience across 273 systematic perturbation configurations.
Spans advanced control tasks including humanoid locomotion and vision-language-action (VLA) environments.
code:
import robust_rllib

# Initialize a robust RL trainer with unified perturbation specs
trainer = robust_rllib.make_trainer(
    algorithm="RobustPPO",
    env_id="HumanoidVLA-v1",
    perturbation_config={"type": "action_noise", "severity": 0.2}
)
trainer.train(total_timesteps=1000000)
fullAnalysis: RobustRLlib addresses major hurdles in robust reinforcement learning by standardizing algorithm implementations and empirical evaluation. Prior efforts suffered from fragmentation across disparate codebases and inconsistent evaluation protocols, making fair comparison difficult. By providing a unified interface across 17 distinct robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms, the library drastically improves code reusability and accelerates development cycles for AI researchers.\n\nThe library introduces a comprehensive benchmark platform encompassing 273 perturbation configurations spanning sensor noise, environmental shifts, dynamic variations, and adversarial attacks. Systematic testing on complex environments, such as humanoid robotics and vision-language-action agents, provides crucial insight into where contemporary robust RL approaches succeed and where significant performance degradation still occurs.
